questions.question:
Identify the segment in the sentence that contains a grammatical error:
'Neither the manager (A) / nor his assistants was (B) / present at the meeting (C) / yesterday. (D)'
questions.explanation: Subject-Verb Agreement Rule with 'Neither... nor': The verb must agree with the nearer subject. Here, the nearer subject is plural ('his assistants'), so the plural verb 'were' must be used instead of 'was'. Correct sentence: 'Neither the manager nor his assistants were present...'
questions.citation: SSC CGL English — Subject-Verb Proximity Rule

questions.question:
Identify the segment in the sentence that contains an error:
'Scarcely had she stepped (A) / out of the house (B) / than it started raining (C) / heavily. (D)'
questions.explanation: Correlative conjunction pair rule: 'Scarcely / Hardly' is always paired with 'when' or 'before', NEVER with 'than' ('No sooner' takes 'than'). Thus, replace 'than' with 'when'.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate preposition to fill in the blank:
'Doctors advise patients suffering from hypertension to abstain _______ excessive salt intake.'
questions.explanation: The verb 'abstain' takes the fixed preposition 'from' (abstain from something = to deliberately avoid or refrain from doing something).

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate SYNONYM of the given word:
PRAGMATIC
questions.explanation: 'Pragmatic' means dealing with things sensibly and realistically based on practical rather than theoretical considerations. Synonym: Practical / Realistic / Down-to-earth.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate SYNONYM of the given word:
CANDID
questions.explanation: 'Candid' means truthful, straightforward, and sincere in speech without concealment. Synonym: Frank / Outspoken / Forthright.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word:
METICULOUS
questions.explanation: 'Meticulous' means showing great attention to detail; very careful and precise. Its direct antonym is 'Careless' / 'Negligent' / 'Sloppy'.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word:
BENEVOLENT
questions.explanation: 'Benevolent' (bene = good, vol = will) means well-meaning, kindly, and charitable. Its opposite is 'Malevolent' (mal = bad, vol = will), meaning having or showing a wish to do evil to others.
questions.citation: SSC CGL English Vocabulary — Root Words & Antonyms

questions.question:
Select the meaning of the given idiom:
'To burn the midnight oil'
options: To study or work late into the night
To set fire to property intentionally
To wake up early at dawn
questions.explanation: 'To burn the midnight oil' means to read, study, or work late into the night (originating from the historical practice of using an oil lamp to work past sunset).

questions.question:
Select the meaning of the given idiom:
'Bite the bullet'
options: To face an inevitable, unpleasant situation with courage
questions.explanation: 'To bite the bullet' means to bravely endure an unavoidable grim, painful, or difficult circumstance without complaining.

questions.question:
Select the meaning of the given idiom:
'At the eleventh hour'
options: At the very last possible moment
Late in the morning at 11 AM
During a time of extreme happiness
questions.explanation: 'At the eleventh hour' means occurring or done just before it is too late; at the critical final moment.

questions.question:
Select the word which means the same as the group of words given:
'A person who loves, collects, or has a great admiration for books'
questions.explanation: Biblio (book) + phile (lover) = Bibliophile. Philanthropist is a lover of humanity; Polyglot is one who knows many languages.

questions.question:
Select the word which means the same as the group of words given:
'An unselfish regard for or devotion to the welfare of others'
questions.explanation: 'Altruism' is the moral practice of selfless concern for the happiness and wellbeing of other human beings. Egoism is self-interest; Narcissism is excessive self-love.

questions.question:
Select the word which means the same as the group of words given:
'A universal remedy or cure for all diseases and difficulties'
questions.explanation: 'Panacea' (pan = all, akos = cure) refers to a mythical or hypothetical solution or remedy for all diseases, problems, or troubles.

questions.question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word:
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'MISCHIEVOUS' (no 'i' after 'v'). 'Bureaucracy', 'Accommodate' (two c's, two m's), and 'Embarrassment' (two r's, two s's) are all spelled correctly.
questions.citation: SSC CGL English — Commonly Confused Spellings

questions.question: Select the CORRECTLY spelt word:
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'QUESTIONNAIRE' (double 'n', ended with 'aire').
questions.citation: SSC CGL English — Word Spelling Rules

questions.question:
Select the option that will improve the underlined segment of the sentence:
'This laptop is _more superior than_ that one in terms of processing speed.'
questions.explanation: Adjectives of Latin origin ending in '-ior' (superior, inferior, senior, junior, prior, anterior, posterior) are never preceded by 'more' (as they are inherently comparative) and are always followed by the preposition 'to', never 'than'.
questions.citation: SSC CGL English — Degrees of Comparison

questions.question:
Select the option that will improve the underlined segment:
'If I _was_ the Education Minister, I would revamp the examination system.'
questions.explanation: In hypothetical/subjunctive conditional clauses expressing an imaginary or impossible present state ('If I...'), the subjunctive verb 'were' is used for all subjects regardless of person or number.
questions.citation: SSC CGL English — Subjunctive Mood & Conditionals

questions.question:
Select the correct passive form of the given active sentence:
'The municipal corporation has repaired all the potholes on the arterial road.'
options: All the potholes on the arterial road have been repaired by the municipal corporation.
All the potholes on the arterial road were repaired by the municipal corporation.
All the potholes on the arterial road had been repaired by the municipal corporation.
All the potholes on the arterial road are being repaired by the municipal corporation.
questions.explanation: In Present Perfect Active (has/have + V3), the Passive voice is formed using: Object + have/has + been + V3 + by + Subject. Since 'All the potholes' is plural, 'have been repaired' is the exact passive transformation.

questions.question:
Select the correct indirect narration for the given direct sentence:
Ravi said to Priya, 'Where will you go for your summer vacation?'
options: Ravi asked Priya where she would go for her summer vacation.
Ravi asked Priya where will she go for her summer vacation.
Ravi asked Priya that where she would go for her summer vacation.
Ravi enquired Priya where was she going for her summer vacation.
questions.explanation:
Rules for Wh-Interrogative indirect speech:
1. 'said to' changes to 'asked'.
2. No conjunction 'that' is used with wh-questions.
3. The interrogative word order changes to assertive: 'will you go' becomes 'she would go'.
4. Pronouns shift accordingly ('you' -> 'she', 'your' -> 'her').

questions.question:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Pick the option that gives their correct, logical sequence:
P. But modern technology has introduced automated drip irrigation systems that deliver water directly to the plant roots.
Q. Traditional irrigation methods often lead to substantial water wastage through evaporation and surface runoff.
R. Consequently, crop yields improve substantially while conserving precious groundwater resources.
S. Agriculture remains the single largest consumer of freshwater resources worldwide.
questions.explanation: Sentence S introduces the broad topic (freshwater consumption in agriculture). Sentence Q describes the problem with traditional irrigation. Sentence P provides the technological counter-solution ('But modern technology...'). Sentence R concludes with the positive consequences ('Consequently...'). The logical sequence is S, Q, P, R.
questions.citation: SSC CGL English — Paragraph Cohesion & Jumbles

questions.question:
Read the following passage and choose the most appropriate option to fill in blank (1):

'In today's fast-paced digital era, the widespread adoption of artificial intelligence is (1) _______ transformative changes across multiple economic sectors. From automated logistics to precision healthcare, AI tools assist human professionals in processing complex data at remarkable speeds. (2) _______, ethical concerns surrounding algorithmic bias and data privacy remain significant. Policymakers must (3) _______ balanced regulatory frameworks that foster technological innovation while simultaneously (4) _______ the fundamental digital rights of everyday citizens. Only through collective collaboration can society harness the full (5) _______ of this revolutionary technology.'

Select the most appropriate option for blank (1):
questions.explanation: The context requires a verb meaning 'causing', 'propelling', or 'catalyzing' transformative changes. 'Driving' is the most idiomatic and precise collocation with 'transformative changes'.
questions.citation: SSC CGL English — Contextual Vocabulary & Collocations

questions.question:
In the same passage, select the most appropriate option for blank (2):
'From automated logistics to precision healthcare, AI tools assist human professionals in processing complex data at remarkable speeds. (2) _______, ethical concerns surrounding algorithmic bias and data privacy remain significant.'
questions.explanation: The previous sentence highlights positive benefits, while this sentence introduces contrasting challenges/concerns. The adversative connector 'However' is required to mark this contrast.
questions.citation: SSC CGL English — Discourse Markers & Connectors

questions.question:
In the same passage, select the most appropriate option for blank (3):
'Policymakers must (3) _______ balanced regulatory frameworks that foster technological innovation...'
questions.explanation: Frameworks and policies are 'formulated' or 'developed'. 'Formulate' (to create or prepare methodically) fits the role of policymakers perfectly.

questions.question:
In the same passage, select the most appropriate option for blank (4):
'...while simultaneously (4) _______ the fundamental digital rights of everyday citizens.'
questions.explanation: Governments and regulations aim to protect or preserve citizen rights. 'Safeguarding' (defending or protecting from harm) is the positive and grammatically sound participle matching 'while simultaneously'.

questions.question:
In the same passage, select the most appropriate option for blank (5):
'Only through collective collaboration can society harness the full (5) _______ of this revolutionary technology.'
questions.explanation: The phrase 'harness the full potential' is a standard English collocation meaning to fully utilize the latent capabilities and power of an innovation.
